segments.say: You wake, if you can call it waking, to the sound of a long, slow wave. You're lying on soft, pale sand, warm underneath and cool on top, near the edge of a wide, empty beach. The sky overhead is a deep velvet blue, wide and clear, scattered with stars right down to the horizon. And the sea is whispering, over and over, the oldest word there is.

The sand is fine as flour, and it holds the warmth of the day, so that wherever your body touches it, there's a gentle heat. It shapes itself around you, as you lie there, taking the curve of your back, your shoulders, the backs of your legs. You sink into it by just a little, like pressing into a very soft pillow, and the sand is perfectly happy to hold you for as long as you like.

The beach curves away into the dark in both directions, a long pale crescent edged with a thin ribbon of foam. Out on the water, the stars are reflected, trembling a little with each swell. There are no lights on this shore, no buildings, no roads. Only the sea, and the sand, and the sky, and you.

show.cap: A quiet beach under the stars

segments.say: Listen to the waves. Each one begins far out, as a faint swelling in the dark. It travels a long way, gathering itself, and then it rises, and curls, and breaks, with a soft, rolling hush. It spreads out thinly across the sand, glimmering for an instant, and then it slips back, and the next wave is already on its way.

Let your breath follow the waves. As the wave swells, breathe in. As it breaks and slides over the sand, breathe out. There's no need to hurry or to count. The sea has been doing this for longer than there have been people to watch, and it will do it all night. You only need to go along with it, and let it breathe for you.

When a wave slides back down the beach, there's a very faint sound, a kind of whispering sigh, as the water slips through the sand. If you listen closely, it sounds almost like a soft voice saying, let go. Let go. And with each withdrawal, you feel a little more of the day drawing out of you, back into the sea, where it dissolves.
Whatever the day has left on the shore, the tide will quietly carry away.

show.text: Whatever the day left on the shore, the tide will take it.

segments.say: Look at the stars, if you like, and let your eyes go loose, the way you'd look at a candle flame. You don't need to count them. You couldn't, anyway. There are far too many, and far too gentle, and the more you let your gaze relax, the more of them seem to appear, as if the sky were slowly unfolding for you.

A faint breeze comes in from the sea, cool and slightly salty, and brushes across your face. It lifts the very edges of your hair, and cools your forehead, and carries away the last traces of any tension that may have been hiding there. You breathe it in, and it feels clean all the way down.

Your body feels very heavy now, and very warm. Your arms are heavy. Your hands are heavy. Your legs sink into the sand, from the thighs, to the knees, to the feet. You couldn't lift a single finger, and you wouldn't want to. It's a delicious, sleepy heaviness, like being buried in warm, soft, fine snow.

If thoughts rise now, they're as thin as sea foam. They shimmer for a moment, on the surface of your mind, and then they pop, and sink, and disappear. There's no need to catch them. There will always be more foam. And the sea underneath is deep, and dark, and quiet.

It feels as though time has slowed here. The night is very long, and very soft, and nobody is counting the hours. If you were to look at a clock, it would say that only a moment had passed. But your body knows better. Your body knows it has been resting, deeply and well, for a long, long while.

Another wave comes in. And another. Each one a little softer than the last, as though the sea itself were getting sleepy. The foam is thinner. The hush is quieter. And in the spaces between them, the silence is deepening, like warm water filling a bath.

And so you sink a little further, with each slow breath, into the warm and quiet sand, under the wide and quiet stars, beside the wide and quiet sea. Nothing is needed. Nothing is missing. All is well, and all is soft, and all is slow.
